section_summary.extract_value: This section reports factorial invariance tests between women and men for two measures (CEMS and IES-2). For the CEMS, results supported metric, scalar, and strict (strong) invariance: "The invariance test between women and men supported metric, scalar, and strict invariance (strong) for the CEMS, Δχ^2_λ(7) = 12.971, p = 0.073; Δχ^2_I(32) = 44.599, p = 0.069; Δχ^2_{cov/res}(25) = 32.952, p = 0.132." For the IES-2, only metric (weak) invariance was supported: "In the case of IES-2, only metric invariance (weak) was found, Δχ^2_λ(15) = 18.858, p = 0.220; Δχ^2_I(68) = 109.358, p = 0.001; Δχ^2_{cov/res}(53) = 95.025, p < 0.001." No explicit study labels (e.g., 'Study 1') or sample descriptive statistics are provided in this section.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports factorial invariance tests comparing women and men for two scales: the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS) and the Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2). Results indicate CEMS showed metric, scalar, and strict (strong) invariance across genders, whereas IES-2 showed only metric (weak) invariance. The text presents chi-square difference statistics and p-values for each test.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The invariance test between women and men supported metric, scalar, and strict invariance (strong) for the CEMS, \Delta\chi^2_{\lambda}(7) = 12.971, p = 0.073; \Delta\chi^2_{I}(32) = 44.599, p = 0.069; \Delta\chi^2_{\text{cov/res}}(25) = 32.952, p = 0.132. In the case of IES-2, only metric invariance (weak) was found, \Delta\chi^2_{\lambda}(15) = 18.858, p = 0.220; \Delta\chi^2_{I}(68) = 109.358, p = 0.001; \Delta\chi^2_{\text{cov/res}}(53) = 95.025, p < 0.001."
